solutions.LA09-guided1-pixels: GATE_TRY two similarly sized people widely separated, facing opposite outside directions, folded arms, straight mouths. These can suggest distance or unwillingness to interact, but could be separate waiting; no proven quarrel. Caption alone only says waited.
solutions.LA09-guided2-pixels: Left close view foregrounds smiling face and eyes towards viewer; right wide view shows shelves and open floor around small profile May. Both show waiting/choosing-caption context without mandatory reader emotion.
solutions.LA09-guided3-pixels: They arrived from text; actual ARRIVAL pixels show brown patches on both figures and map split with jagged edges. Mud interpretation supported by supplied neutral labels; exact muddy-event cause unknown, creek fall not established.
solutions.LA09-visual-creation: Require drawn far-separated offering pair and close pair both reaching, then a supported possible relationship comparison (offering/helping/sharing versus shared interest/cooperation). Caption names friends, so do not claim friendship uncertain there; identities/history/box contents remain unknown.
solutions.LA09-model-pixels: MEETING facing smiling similar-size figures reach shared box, supports cooperation. GATE_MODEL relative size and explicit dotted gaze line connect larger looking down/smaller looking up; extended arm points, possible authority without cruelty. VIEWER face large direct gaze vs small profile turned to right/away in open space. Actual diagrams inspected individually at rendered PNG scale; source-specific content consistent.
solutions.LA10-card1: Card length 9 centimetres; strip width 3 millimetres. Width 4 centimetres is optional extra correct fact, not substituted for asked strip width.
solutions.LA10-card2: Characters Dot/duck and frog; setting noon beside pond; plot Dot loses feather, frog finds, Dot places in nest. Accept connected subset if prompt allows summary.
solutions.LA10-card3: Light feather could mean not heavy OR pale in colour; bird/feather alone does not distinguish senses. Second light = illumination supported by see. FIRST SENSE AMBIGUOUS: accept both supported possibilities or clarify low weight via lifting/weighing clue.
solutions.LA10-card4: Redraw = draw again, re- again; helpful clue sentence expresses useful aid. This specific replacement is already visible in prompt, a supported demonstration not blind scored answer.
solutions.LA10-freshcheck: Label 7 centimetres long; setting at night in tent; plot losing torch/finding in bag. Bright torch=strong light, clue lit tent; bright idea=clever/good idea, context idea. Rewrite replaces write again using re-.
